title: Machine learning helps identify experimentally synthesized cobalt superalloys
summary: A random-forest model trained on first-principles formation and decomposition energies screened more than 150,000 proposed gamma-prime compositions. Domain screening and CALPHAD narrowed the set; researchers synthesized two selected Co-based gamma/gamma-prime alloy systems and characterized their microstructures. The measured compositions differ from nominal targets, and preliminary hardness values were below the cited conventional comparator. Engine performance was not demonstrated. Count the study once.
organization: Xiamen University; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen

source_review.scope: Primary npj Computational Materials article page, abstract, indexed results and author metadata.

evidence.tested: Researchers synthesized and characterized two screened Co-based alloy systems; XRD and electron microscopy support reported microstructures and preliminary hardness was measured.
evidence.unknown: Nominal and measured compositions differ; preliminary hardness was below the cited conventional comparator; no engine performance or independent replication was reported.
evidence.ai_role: A random-forest model trained on DFT energies screened candidate gamma-prime compositions; domain experts and CALPHAD then narrowed candidates for synthesis.
